BATCH J · BOARD 3 OF 5

Accessibility audit — a legal requirement, measured

Screens 14–18. The European Accessibility Act applies from 28 June 2025 and the harmonised standard is EN 301 549, which incorporates WCAG 2.1 AA. Three of the most complex screens already designed are audited below with real numbers — measured ratios, numbered focus order, a traced keyboard-only path, listed accessible names and measured target sizes. Failures are listed as failures.

The design system already forces most of this: near-black on off-white gives 17.4:1, focus-visible is a mandatory 2px signal ring at 2px offset, and nothing ships below 11px. What an audit adds is the cases the tokens cannot decide — focus order in a three-pane layout, the accessible name of an icon-only button, and whether a scatter plot means anything to a screen reader.
14 AUDIT 1 · THE QUESTION COMPOSER 1440 × 700 · C1 screen 1 · the most complex input surface in the product

11Outcome radio group · one stoparrows

13Review and post
14Retrieval panel · after the form
The retrieval panel is last on purpose. It updates as you type; if it sat in the tab order before the post button, a screen-reader user would be pushed through changing suggestions every time they moved. It is an aria-live="polite" region announced on change, and reachable directly with a landmark jump.

KEYBOARD-ONLY PATH · TRACED END TO END
Post a complete question without a mouse: Tab ×2 → type title → Tab ×2 → type body → Tab ×6 → fill conditions → Tab → → to pick outcome → Tab ×2 → Enter. Or ⌘↵ from any field. 14 stops, no traps, and Escape always closes the quality assistant without losing the draft.
FAILURE 1 OF 3 · OPEN
The LaTeX preview has no text alternative. A rendered equation is an image to a screen reader. Fix: expose the source as the accessible name and offer MathML output. Owner: composer team · blocks AA on 1.1.1
COVERAGES01 · S02 · S03 · F01 · F24EN 301 549 · WCAG 2.1 AA · 1 open failure on this screen
14b AUDIT 2 AND 3 · UPLOAD · INSTITUTIONAL DASHBOARD 760 × 640
DATASET UPLOADE1 screens 1–6 →1 FAILURE
Drag-and-drop has a keyboard equivalent. The dropzone is a button; Enter opens the file picker. 2.1.1 satisfied — this is the single most commonly failed pattern in upload UIs.
Upload progress is role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow, announced at 25% intervals rather than continuously.
Validation errors use aria-describedby on the field, not a summary at the top. 3.3.1 and 3.3.3.
The 5-step wizard is a nav with aria-current="step"; step state is never colour alone.
FAILURE 2 · the privacy-scan result table. Findings are conveyed by row background alone at small sizes. Fix: add a text status column. 1.4.1 use of colour
INSTITUTIONAL DASHBOARDI2 screen 4 →1 FAILURE
Every chart has a table. A "view as table" control sits beside each figure and the table is the accessible name target — not a generated alt string trying to describe a trend.
The red caution banner is role="note", first in the reading order after the heading, and announced before any figure.
The department table has scope on headers and a caption naming the period, so a row read aloud is self-describing.
Zoom to 200% and 400% reflows without horizontal scrolling · 1.4.10.
FAILURE 3 · the four-year bar pair. Two series distinguished by colour with no pattern or label. Fix: direct labels on the final bar of each series. 1.4.1

18 ACCESSIBILITY STATEMENT (S03) — PUBLISHED 640 × 640 · required, and honest
PUBLIC ACCESSIBILITY STATEMENT
SciCollab is committed to meeting EN 301 549 and WCAG 2.1 level AA. This statement was last reviewed on 2026-09-10 and is updated whenever an audit closes.
CONFORMANCE STATUS
Partially conformant. Most of the product meets AA. Three known failures are listed below with a target date. We do not claim full conformance while any are open — a statement that overclaims is worse than one that admits a gap.

THE HONEST NOTE · 2 UNSOLVED IN PRINCIPLE
The molecular and genomic viewers are interactive 3D and dense sequence surfaces. We provide a full data table and a text summary for both, but we do not claim the interactive view itself is equivalent for a non-sighted user. We are not aware of a solved approach in any comparable product, and we would rather say so than tick a box.
FEEDBACK AND ENFORCEMENT
accessibility@scicollab.org · we answer within 5 working days. If you are not satisfied you may contact the national enforcement body in your member state, named and linked on the full page.
